whatItIs.title: What it is
whatItIs.wide: The cerebellar tonsils, the lowest part of the cerebellum, extend below the foramen magnum, the opening at the base of the skull. The cerebellum helps control balance and coordination. Often, the malformation is related to the back and lower part of the skull being smaller or having another shape, which leaves little room for the brain. Less often, it appears later in life from other causes.
whatItIs.narrow: The cerebellar tonsils, the lowest part of the cerebellum, extend below the opening at the base of the skull. Often, the malformation is related to the back and lower part of the skull being smaller or having another shape, which leaves little room for the brain. Less often, it appears later in life from other causes.

whoHasIt.title: Who has it
whoHasIt.wide: Most people are born with the skull differences that cause it. Some never have symptoms; others notice them for the first time in adolescence or in adulthood.
whoHasIt.narrow: Most people are born with the skull differences that cause it. Some never have symptoms; others notice them for the first time in adolescence or in adulthood.

howFound.title: How it is detected
howFound.wide: Usually, with an MRI and a medical exam; sometimes, by chance, during a scan for another reason. The doctor reviews the images together with your symptoms.
howFound.narrow: Usually, with an MRI and a medical exam; sometimes, by chance.

feel.title: What can be felt
feel.intro: Chiari is different in each person, and many people with type I do not have any symptoms.

classic.wide: The classic symptom is a headache in the back of the head that appears after coughing, sneezing or straining.
classic.narrow: The classic symptom is a headache in the back of the head after coughing, sneezing or straining.

symptoms.wide: Numbness or tingling in the hands and feet
symptoms.narrow: Numbness or tingling in hands and feet

symptoms.wide: Weakness or difficulty making fine movements with the hands
symptoms.narrow: Weakness or difficulty making fine movements with the hands

symptoms.wide: Problems breathing or sleeping, such as sleep apnea
A curvature of the spine (scoliosis), especially in children

feel.noSymptoms: Many people with type I do not have any symptoms.

items.wide: Chiari is a difference in structure that can affect balance, the nerves and the flow of cerebrospinal fluid, not just cause headaches.
items.narrow: It can also affect balance, the nerves and the flow of cerebrospinal fluid.

items.wide: Traditionally, doctors use as a cutoff about 5 mm below the opening. How far the cerebellar tonsils go down does not always match how a person feels. Some people with a clear descent have no symptoms, and some with less than 5 mm do have them. Doctors also look at the shape of the cerebellar tonsils, the flow of cerebrospinal fluid and whether there is a syrinx.
items.narrow: How far the cerebellar tonsils go down does not always match how a person feels. Doctors also look at their shape, the flow of the fluid and whether there is a syrinx.

explorer.title: 3D Explorer

typical.label: Typical anatomy
typical.note: The cerebellar tonsils usually sit at the level of the dotted line that crosses the skull opening or above it (a few millimeters below can still be normal), and the cerebrospinal fluid flows freely around them.
typical.noteShort: The cerebellar tonsils usually sit at the level of the skull opening or above (a few millimeters below can be normal); the fluid flows freely.

chiari.label: Chiari I
chiari.note: The cerebellar tonsils extend below the opening, at least about 5 mm by the usual definition. In a study of 160 people with Chiari I, the average was about 12 mm, but it ranged from 5 to 25 mm, and the number by itself does not decide who needs surgery. They often have a pointed shape instead of rounded. The fluid space behind them is often reduced, and in many people the flow of the fluid becomes slower or is blocked there.
chiari.noteShort: The cerebellar tonsils extend below the opening and often reduce the fluid space; in many people the flow becomes slower there.

syrinx.label: Chiari I with syrinx
syrinx.note: A syrinx is a fluid-filled cavity inside the spinal cord. It often appears together with Chiari, especially in the part of the spinal cord that is in the neck.
syrinx.noteShort: A fluid-filled cavity formed inside the spinal cord.

surgery.label: After decompression
surgery.note: Surgeons remove a small piece of bone from the back of the skull opening and, often, the back of the first vertebra. Often they also open the membrane that covers the brain and put a patch on it to give more room to the cerebrospinal fluid. The cerebellar tonsils often rise only partly. Surgery improves or stabilizes symptoms in most people, although damage that already happened may not reverse completely, and some people need more than one operation. Results vary, and surgery is not right for everyone.
surgery.noteShort: Bone is removed from the back of the opening to give room. Most people improve or stabilize, but results vary, some need another operation and surgery is not right for everyone.

explorer.partsButton: Parts list · tap a part of the model

parts.name: Brain [Cerebro]
parts.text: The largest part of the brain [encéfalo], in charge of thinking, movement and the senses.

parts.name: Corpus callosum
parts.text: A thick band of nerve fibers that joins the left and right halves of the brain.

parts.name: Cerebellum
parts.text: The back part of the brain [encéfalo] that helps control balance and coordination.

parts.name: Fourth ventricle
parts.text: A small fluid-filled space between the brainstem and the cerebellum, through which the cerebrospinal fluid passes.

parts.name: Brainstem
parts.text: Joins the brain with the spinal cord and controls automatic functions such as breathing, heart rate and swallowing.

parts.name: Cerebellar tonsil
parts.text: The two lowest parts of the cerebellum. In Chiari, they extend below the opening at the base of the skull and often have a pointed (peg-like) shape instead of rounded. In reality, they are just to each side of the midline and often go down unevenly; the model shows them at their lowest point, where they are measured on MRI.

parts.name: Foramen magnum
parts.text: The opening at the base of the skull where the brainstem becomes the spinal cord.

parts.name: Spinal cord
parts.text: Carries signals between the brain and the rest of the body.

parts.name: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)
parts.text: A clear fluid that cushions the brain and the spinal cord. With each heartbeat, it moves back and forth between the skull and the spinal canal.

parts.name: C2 vertebra
parts.text: The second bone of the neck. Its upward projection, the odontoid process, is just in front of the spinal cord.

parts.name: Syrinx
parts.text: A fluid-filled cavity inside the spinal cord. It often appears together with Chiari, especially in the part of the spinal cord that is in the neck.

parts.name: Bone removed
parts.text: Surgeons remove a small piece of bone from the back of the skull opening and, often, the back of the first vertebra.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.short: In short: Open Chiari does not know who you are, does not use cookies and never collects health information.

counted.before: To show the totals on the
counted.after: , the site counts visits and a few actions: opening the 3D model, creating an Explain It link and opening a study's listing. For counting, Open Chiari's own counter is used, which does not use cookies or create a profile of you. Your browser sends only the name of the action, and the counter adds 1 to a total. It does not save your address, device, browser, country, the page you come from or the link. When the 3D model is shown on another website, the address of that site is noted, so that the Impact page can count the sites that use it.

never.text: No accounts, sign-ins, names or email addresses.
Your note goes in the message you send, not in the link. The link only contains the chosen view, after the #. Browsers do not send that part to our server, and the counter never receives it.

steps.title: Meet the model
steps.text: This view shows the head and neck cut in half, along the midline. The cerebellum helps control balance and coordination. The foramen magnum is the opening at the base of the skull where the brainstem becomes the spinal cord.

steps.title: Typical anatomy
steps.text: The cerebellar tonsils usually sit at the level of the dotted line that crosses the skull opening or above it (a few millimeters below can still be normal), and the cerebrospinal fluid flows freely around them.

steps.title: The cerebellar tonsils are too low
steps.text: The dotted line crosses the opening at the base of the skull. In Chiari, the cerebellar tonsils, the lowest part of the cerebellum, extend below it, as the blue bracket shows.

steps.title: How the fluid flows
steps.text: Cerebrospinal fluid is a clear fluid that cushions the brain and the spinal cord. With each heartbeat, it moves back and forth between the skull and the spinal canal. In Chiari, the cerebellar tonsils extend below the line (blue bracket) and often reduce the space where the fluid should pass. The red marks show where the flow is often restricted.

steps.title: A syrinx
steps.text: A syrinx is a fluid-filled cavity inside the spinal cord. It often appears together with Chiari, especially in the part of the spinal cord that is in the neck.

NCT06502431.summary: The researchers want to understand how cerebrospinal fluid and blood move in the head and neck in Chiari I. They use a special MRI that measures flow and compare adults with and without symptoms with people without Chiari.
NCT06502431.whatYoudDo: Additional flow studies that are added to an MRI, on a single day. For adults 18 to 50 years old without previous surgeries of the brain or spine and without a history of other conditions of the nerves or of the heart (ask the study team what counts). It is not for people who cannot have an MRI or for people who are pregnant or breastfeeding. People with Chiari are invited after a neurosurgery consultation at the Amiens hospital, and the team re-reviews the images to confirm the Chiari I.

NCT06724029.summary: The researchers want to know what predicts how people do after a surgery of the brain or spine, in many conditions, among them Chiari I. The study does not change anyone's treatment; it only collects health information before the surgery and after.
NCT06724029.whatYoudDo: Your health information is collected before the surgery and during the later follow-up; the frequency and the duration depend on the condition, and the listing does not say. For adults who will have neurosurgery at one of the hospitals in Italy that are still accepting new participants (the official listing shows which ones).
